title: Microsoft Purview: higher auto-labeling limits for SharePoint sites and simulation, plus new reporting
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout facts, increased limits and corrected reporting navigation are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge differing Microsoft licensing guidance and reconcile the governance checklist with the controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is September CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) only, not GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: This Microsoft Purview change expands auto-labeling scale, SharePoint targeting and reporting.
claims.quote: These enhancements expand support for larger SharePoint scopes, improve policy management flexibility, and provide richer visibility into auto-labeling activity.

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified on 11 November 2026 at 00:52:46.
The notice increases simulation capacity from 4 million to 20 million items.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling simulation capacity will increase from 4 million items to 20 million items.

claims.claim: The notice permits selecting up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to select up to 1,000 individual SharePoint sites when configuring policies.

claims.claim: The notice increases adaptive scope support to 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes will support up to 50,000 SharePoint sites per policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice announces SiteTemplate filtering of SharePoint sites during policy configuration.
claims.quote: SharePoint sites can be filtered using the SiteTemplate property during policy configuration.

claims.claim: The notice adds audit and reporting summaries of sensitive information types detected when labels are applied.
claims.quote: Audit and reporting experiences will provide additional visibility, including summaries of the Sensitive Information Types (SITs) detected when labels are applied.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice announces a 30-day chart showing files processed each day.
claims.quote: A new 30-day processing chart will display the number of files processed each day, helping administrators monitor policy throughput and activity over time.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The enhancements are on by default.
claims.quote: These enhancements are on by default and will be available automatically as the rollout reaches your organization.

claims.claim: The enhancements become available automatically as rollout reaches an organisation.
claims.quote: These enhancements are on by default and will be available automatically as the rollout reaches your organization.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing auto-labeling policies continue functioning without modification.
claims.quote: Existing auto-labeling policies will continue to function without modification.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: action
claims.claim: Microsoft says no action is required.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft expects no impact to end users.
claims.quote: There is no expected impact to end users.

claims.claim: The notice gives public preview as beginning early September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-September 2026.
claims.quote: Public Preview: Available beginning early September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-September 2026.

claims.claim: Worldwide general availability is scheduled to begin and complete in mid-November 2026, previously late October.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

claims.claim: Microsoft updated the notice's timeline on 3 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft describes increased processing capacity rather than a change to labeling behaviour.
claims.quote: The change expands processing capacity rather than changing labeling behavior.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn documents simulation support for up to 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files.

claims.claim: A policy matching more than 20,000,000 files in simulation cannot be turned on until it is narrowed and simulation rerun.
claims.quote: If more than this number of files are matched from an auto-labeling policy, you can't turn on the policy to apply the labels. In this case, you must reconfigure the auto-labeling policy so that fewer files are matched, and rerun simulation.

claims.claim: The 20,000,000 matched-file maximum applies only to simulation, not an already enabled policy.
claims.quote: This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on to apply sensitivity labels.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Portal policies can explicitly include or exclude up to 1,000 SharePoint sites per policy.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites, or up to 100 explicitly included or excluded OneDrive individual users or groups.

claims.claim: For auto-labeling policies, a SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per policy.
claims.quote: For auto-labeling policies, a SharePoint adaptive scope supports up to 50,000 sites per policy.

claims.claim: Learn's Labeling activity overview chart covers the last 30 days with separate successful and failed series.
claims.quote: Its Labeling activity overview chart has separate successful and failed series for the last 30 days.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy on after simulation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Review pages require Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Information Protection Admin or Information Protection Analyst.
claims.quote:
To view the review pages, you need one of the following roles:

- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Information Protection Admin
- Information Protection Analyst

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: When administrative units are selected in a policy, SharePoint must use All rather than Included or Excluded.
claims.quote:
For organizations that are using administrative units and selected in the policy:

- For SharePoint, you can't use the Included or Excluded options and must use the All default selection.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Service-side auto-labeling applies labels without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: The tenant-wide throughput ceiling is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per day across all policies.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The daily throughput ceiling is not a guaranteed rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Simulation requires auditing for Microsoft 365 to be turned on.
claims.quote:
Simulation mode:

- Auditing for Microsoft 365 must be turned on.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited Learn page includes service-side auto-labeling with Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote: Client-side auto-labeling (Office apps) | Sensitivity label configuration → Auto-labeling for files and emails page | Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited Learn page includes service-side auto-labeling with Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone)

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The cited Learn page includes service-side auto-labeling with Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance.
claims.quote: Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) | Microsoft Purview portal → Information Protection → Policies → Auto-labeling policies | Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited Learn page includes service-side auto-labeling with standalone Azure Information Protection Premium P2.
claims.quote: Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone) ... Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) ... Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above
claims.fix: After the licensing paragraph, add: 'Microsoft documentation differs: the Microsoft Purview service description says automatic or policy-based labeling requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance, while the auto-labeling page also lists standalone Azure Information Protection Premium P2. The service description also requires AIP P1 to be assigned when AIP P2 is assigned.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-information-protection-sensitivity-labeling.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model refers to service-side auto-labeling being included in the listed eligible licences.
claims.quote: Surface | Configured in | Included with ... Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) ... Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Separate licensing for these enhancements is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling reporting Insights licensing requirements license meter pay as you go; opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, auto-label-insights-tab, purview-billing-models and Microsoft Purview service description. No separate enhancement licence stated.

claims.claim: No separate meter is published for these Microsoft 365 auto-labeling enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling reporting Insights licensing requirements license meter pay as you go; opened purview-billing-models and apply-sensitivity-label-automatically. No enhancement meter stated; Information Protection PAYG covers non-Microsoft 365 sources.

claims.claim: The supplied notice mentions no charge.
claims.quote: These enhancements are on by default and will be available automatically as the rollout reaches your organization. Existing auto-labeling policies will continue to function without modification.

claims.claim: A different licence requirement specifically for the new reports has not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling reporting Insights licensing requirements license meter pay as you go; opened auto-label-insights-tab, apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and Microsoft Purview service description. No distinct licence for these policy-level reports stated.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is unavailable in some regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is hidden in the Purview portal where a tenant cannot support auto-labeling.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies are listed under Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The policy creation path is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > Create auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select + Create auto-labeling policy.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports the printed Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy call to add explicitly selected SharePoint sites in test mode.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation $spoLocations -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes are configured in Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Name <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -SharePointAdaptiveScopes <AdaptiveScope> -ApplySensitivityLabel <Label> -Mode TestWithoutNotifications.
claims.quote: To target more than 1,000 SharePoint sites, associate an existing SharePoint adaptive scope with the policy by using the -SharePointAdaptiveScopes parameter (or -SharePointAdaptiveScopesException for exclusions) with New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy.

claims.claim: Creating an adaptive scope requires the Scope Manager role.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Compliance Administrator is among the role groups containing Scope Manager.
claims.quote:
The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups:

- Compliance Administrator

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Associating an adaptive scope replaces static enumeration with dynamic membership rather than increasing the portal limit.
claims.quote: This doesn't increase the portal limit; instead, it replaces static site enumeration with dynamic adaptive-scope membership.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises preserving simulation results needed for comparison before editing or rerunning a policy.
claims.quote: Before you edit an auto-labeling policy or run simulation again, export any available results that you need for later comparison.

claims.claim: For enabled policies, Insights is available when SharePoint or OneDrive is included.
claims.quote: Enforcement: The tab is available only when the policy includes SharePoint or OneDrive. ... The tab isn't available for disabled policies or Exchange-only policies that are turned on.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: SIT summaries are shown on Insights in the policy details panel.
claims.quote: In the policy details panel, select Insights. ... Top 10 sensitive info types ... The table lists the sensitive information types (SITs) most frequently detected when this policy applied labels during the last 30 days.

claims.claim: View details > Overview opens the daily 30-day Labeling activity overview chart in the newer full review experience.
claims.quote: For the daily trend, select View details and open Overview in the newer full review experience. Labeling activity overview shows separate successful and failed operation counts for the last 30 days, not distinct-file counts.

claims.claim: The policy review path is Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: The newer label-application review experience has Overview, Labeled items and Labeling failures tabs.
claims.quote: The newer review page has separate Overview, Labeled items, and Labeling failures tabs.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a separate tenant switch for the new reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling new reporting Insights enable disable tenant setting switch PowerShell; opened auto-label-insights-tab, apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, New-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy and Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy. No separate reporting switch documented.

claims.claim: No new role is described for these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scalability reporting enhancements Insights roles permissions new role; read role prerequisites in apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and auto-label-insights-tab, plus MC1469958. No new enhancement-specific role described.

claims.claim: The table covers general policy targeting controls rather than rollout switches.
claims.quote: Administrators can utilize expanded SharePoint site selection limits, adaptive scope limits, and SiteTemplate filtering during policy configuration.

claims.claim: The governance checklist checks controls not represented by rows in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Confirm that the roles you need are assigned'; 'Check whether any policy ... uses administrative units'; 'Test any enlarged policy in simulation'; 'Confirm auditing is on'. Table rows cover only explicit SharePoint selection and adaptive scopes.
claims.fix: The role-assignment, administrative-unit, simulation and auditing checklist steps have no corresponding control rows. To reconcile the checklist without adding rows, remove those four checklist bullets; retain their already documented prerequisites and advice in Risk assessment.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents SiteTemplate as an adaptive-scope property for including or excluding site types.
claims.quote: you can use the indexed site property SiteTemplate to include or exclude specific site types.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating reporting and operational processes to use the new reporting.
claims.quote: Update reporting and operational processes to leverage the new Sensitive Information Type reporting details and processing throughput metrics.
